title: Evaluating the clinical effectiveness of sodium bicarbonate for critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and acute kidney injury
official: Evaluating the clinical effectiveness of sodium bicarbonate for critically ill patients with metabolic acidosis and acute kidney injury
summary: Main objective: To investigate the effect of sodium bicarbonate on major adverse kidney events at day 90

interventions.name:
Elektrolyt-Infusionslösung 153
Gesamtkationen/-anionen 153 mval/l,
Infusionslösung zur intravenösen Anwendung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult ≥ 18 years
2. Critically ill patients (requiring treatment on an Intensive Care Unit or Intermediate Care Unit)
3. Metabolic acidosis, defined as all of the following: a.	Arterial pH ≤7.25 b.	PaCO2 < 6.5kPa (<49 mmHg) c.	Standard bicarbonate ≤20 mmol/L d.	Standard Base Excess <-2
4. AKI stage 2 or 3 of the KDIGO classification
5. Written informed consent of the patient or legal representative or authorized representative or emergency inclusion (according to Article 35 EU-Regulation 536/2014)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Respiratory acidosis (acute or chronic)
2. Symptomatic hypocalcaemia (Ionized calcium <1.05 mmol/L)
3. Hypernatremia (plasma sodium >150 mmol/L)
4. Severe hypokalemia (potassium <3.0 mmol/L)
5. Patients on KRT, or KRT immediately indicated and treating clinician(s) unwilling to defer
6. Deemed unsuitable for KRT
7. High output stoma/ileostomy
8. Percutaneous biliary drainage
9. End stage kidney failure defined as documented eGFR <15ml/min/1.73m2 prior to onset of this acute illness or end stage kidney disease (ESKD) on dialysi
10. Known renal tubular acidosis
11. Diabetic ketoacidosis
12. High anion gap acid poisoning (e.g. polyethylene glycol (PEG), aspirin, methanol)
